shardDecision: 63 files and 5,755 changed lines — far past one pass. Split into the 5 shards the slice's How-to-shard section gives, dispatched to code-reviewer-open on opus in one message, balanced by changed lines and disjoint: S1 the API integration suite plus 14 one-line e2e edits (15 files, ~1,170), S2 the server heart — home/entry services, types, schema, migration, fixture — plus 7 more e2e edits (15, ~1,075), S3 the HTTP surface, the validation package and the two shared web files (10, ~978), S4 the portal e2e suite plus the two new pages and the e2e specs the landing move touched (12, ~1,098), S5 the client half of the home screen and its settings form (6, ~1,189). I kept the five spec-bundle files (246 lines) for myself, because the requirement and boundary sweeps are read from the document and not from the diff.

blastRadius: The landing move is the only thing this change does outside /portal, and it is clean. Every one of the 30 e2e files that waited on `**/members` now waits on /\/org\/[^/]+\/?$/, which cannot match a /members URL ([^/]+ spans no second segment and \/?$ anchors), so the rewritten waits still fail if the landing does not move. The four remaining `waitForURL('**/members')` calls are all correct and unrelated: signup.spec.ts:16 is the signup redirect (SignupForm.tsx:101, which this spec's Out of Scope leaves alone), request-topics.spec.ts:372 is an unauthorized reader's router.replace, time-tracking.spec.ts:116 and invitation.spec.ts:57 follow a real navigation. The sidebar's new row is pushed after the client-contact early return, so a contact never gets it, and OrgLayout notFound()s a contact on the organization root — the two agree. `packages/validation/src/roles.ts` gains two capability values and four matrix entries and removes nothing, so no existing caller changes. `e2e/tests/ui-invariants.ts` gains `expectSharedEdge` and edits nothing existing. No shipped contract is changed that the spec did not ask for; the one candidate — the rail's logo still addressing /members while the landing is now the root — is recorded as note N9 for a person, because the spec's own Screens section says the login form 'changes its destination and nothing else'. Role transition: every new authorization decision goes through `hasCapability`/`normalizeRole`, which map the stored `member` to `user`, and TC-01-INT-02 exercises the legacy value — CR-04 clean.

findings.rule: specs/portal/01-home.md REQ-01-026 — the window the feed reads
findings.claim: the window's end is the caller's local calendar date read as a UTC day, so for every caller in a zone behind UTC the feed and the entry page drop everything that happened in the latest hours of the caller's own today

witness.detail: `todayInTimeZone` (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:639) formats the instant in the caller's Account.timezone and answers a 'YYYY-MM-DD' local date. `computePortalWindow` then does `new Date(`${today}T23:59:59.999Z`)` — the end of that date in UTC. For a caller in America/Los_Angeles (UTC-7 in September), at 20:00 local on 2026-09-08 the instant is 2026-09-09T03:00:00Z; today is '2026-09-08' and end is 2026-09-08T23:59:59.999Z, which is three hours in the PAST. A vacancy created at 17:30 local (2026-09-09T00:30:00Z) has createdAt > end, so deriveVacancyEntries' `createdAt: { gte: start, lte: end }` (portal-feed.service.ts:223) excludes it from the feed, and portal-entry.service.ts:83 throws NotFoundException for its entry page — while a colleague in UTC or ahead of it reads the same row normally. deriveMemberEntries (line 169) and deriveProjectEntries (line 255) clip identically. REQ-01-026 requires the window to end at 'the caller's own today', which for that caller ends at 2026-09-09T07:00:00Z. Both S2 and S3 found this independently; a UTC-run integration suite cannot observe it, because under UTC `end` is always in the future.

findings.suggestedFix: end the window at the caller's own end-of-day instant in their zone (or clamp to `now`) rather than at the UTC end of the local date string; the 365-day start shifts with it and Edge case 3's inclusive boundary must still hold

findings.rule: specs/portal/01-home.md REQ-01-056 — no roster where they may not
findings.claim: a reader who may not see the roster is answered `"members": null` rather than a body with no `members` key, so the withholding is visible in the response — and the integration case asserts the wrong side of it

witness.detail: REQ-01-056 (specs/portal/01-home.md:365): 'IF the reader holds neither, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL omit the members from that entry page.' The contrast with its sibling is deliberate and stated: REQ-01-055's clientName is 'null rather than absent' precisely so the two cases cannot be told apart, while the roster is to be omitted. `members` is initialised `null` at portal-entry.service.ts:304 and returned unconditionally at :343, so the body carries `"members": null`; a reader who MAY see the roster of a project with no assignees is answered `"members": []`, so the two are distinguishable and §Screens 'Q3 answered, trimmed — Nothing states that anything was withheld' is broken. The method's own comment at :278 says the field is 'omitted (never nulled) otherwise', which is not what it does — code arguing its own exception. apps/api/test/portal.spec.ts:1127 then writes `expect(unassignedPage.body.members).toBeNull()`, which passes only for the present-and-null shape and fails for the omitted one, so the test certifies the requirement's negation. Found independently by S1 and S2.

findings.suggestedFix: spread the key in only when `canSeeRoster` (`...(canSeeRoster ? { members } : {})`), make `members` optional on PortalEntryDetailDto, and change portal.spec.ts:1127 to `expect('members' in unassignedPage.body).toBe(false)`

findings.claim: TC-01-INT-09's Expected Result cannot be reached from its own Steps under REQ-01-026, and the implementation settled the contradiction silently by writing a different case

witness.detail: Two statements, both quoted. specs/portal/01-home.cases.md TC-01-INT-09: Steps — 'Backdate the remaining one's joinedAt by two years and a day through the fixture'; Expected Result — 'One member-joined entry for the remaining member, at its backdated moment, and two member-anniversary entries for it with detail.years 1 and 2.' specs/portal/01-home.md:220 REQ-01-026 — 'THE SYSTEM SHALL derive entries from source rows whose moment falls in the 365 days ending at the caller's own today.' With joinedAt at today-731 days the joining moment is outside the window, so no member-joined entry for that member can exist; TC-01-INT-12 states the same reading explicitly ('The 366-day one's is absent, and its first anniversary … is present'). The Y=1 anniversary at today-366 is outside too, so two anniversaries are also unreachable. The implementer resolved it rather than raising it: apps/api/test/portal.spec.ts:703 backdates by exactly two years, not two years and a day, and :700-701 assert `expect(memberJoined).toHaveLength(1)` with `memberJoined[0].subject.id === admin.membershipId` — the admin's own joining, which is the opposite of the case's stated subject. A person must decide whether the case or REQ-01-026 moves; neither this gate nor the implementer may settle it.

findings.suggestedFix: restate TC-01-INT-09's Steps and Expected Result so they agree with REQ-01-026 and TC-01-INT-12, then rewrite the test to whatever the document then says

findings.claim: six user-facing failure sentences are written inline in app code across four files, where every other area of this product exports its failure text from packages/validation

witness.detail: `grep -rn "Something went wrong" apps/web/app apps/web/src --include=*.tsx` returns exactly seven hits and all seven are this change's own files: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/page.tsx:147, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/PortalFeed.tsx:364, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/news/[entryId]/page.tsx:255, and apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/settings/portal/page.tsx:87, :96, :116, :123. `grep -rn "went wrong" packages/validation/src/*.ts` returns the convention they break: SIGNING_PROVIDER settings.saveFailed (signing-providers.ts:78), HOLIDAY toastServerError (holiday-messages.ts:29), ENVELOPE_MESSAGES.generic (envelopes.ts:221), PROFILE_MESSAGES.generic.networkError (autofill.ts:551), documents.ts:126, and four more in index.ts. PORTAL_MESSAGES (packages/validation/src/portal.ts:8-19) already carries this spec's nine other client-only strings and carries no failure key, so none of these six sentences exists anywhere a test, the server or another screen can read it. settings/portal/page.tsx:116 also discards the server's own message: the contract gives PUT .../portal/settings a 422 PORTAL_MESSAGES.groupsInvalid body and the `!response.ok` branch replaces it with the inline string.

findings.suggestedFix: add load/save failure keys to PORTAL_MESSAGES and render them at all four call sites; surface the server's message where the response carries one

findings.rule: ui-invariants UI-07 — one value with two sources
findings.claim: the feed decides what day it is from the browser clock while the rest of the same screen decides it from the server's month.today, so one value has two sources that disagree on screen

witness.detail: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/page.tsx passes `today={homeState.data.month.today}` into PortalRequestsPanel (:160) and PortalTimeOffPanel, and draws the greeting from `formatGreetingDate(month.today)`; PortalFeed is passed no today at all (:165-168). `dayLabel` (PortalFeed.tsx:100-108) computes `startOfDay(new Date())` from the device clock and `formatRelativeTime` (:86-97) uses `Date.now()` and an Intl.DateTimeFormat with no timeZone. Caller with Account.timezone America/Los_Angeles, device set to Europe/Warsaw, at 2026-11-09T00:30 Warsaw: REQ-01-010 makes the server answer month.today '2026-11-08', so the greeting reads 8 November and every holiday row's 'in N days' counts from 8 November, while a feed entry at 2026-11-08T22:00:00Z — 14:00 on the caller's own 8 November — is captioned 'Earlier this week' because dayLabel's device-derived today is 9 November. The screen states the caller's today twice and gives two answers. portal-types.ts:113-122 records this exact hazard as the reason the greeting must not use `new Date()`.

findings.suggestedFix: pass month.today and month.timezone into PortalFeed and resolve both the day boundary and the weekday in the caller's zone

contracts §What the screen borrows: '| Preloader (§23) | role="status", findable by a test | Each of Q1 and Q2 draws its own |'. PortalFeed.tsx:357-360 renders `

findings.rule: ui-craft — a request lifecycle where every path ends
findings.claim: a failed settings load leaves the screen waiting forever: the render branch is keyed on `!groups`, which the failure path never fills, so the screen's own state claims a request that has ended is still running

witness.detail: An admin opens /org/{orgId}/settings/portal and GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/settings answers 500, or the connection drops. `load` (lines 84-98) calls setError, setLoading(false) and returns without ever assigning `groups`, so `groups` stays null. The render at :141 is `loading || !groups ? <Preloader/> : rows`, still true — so the screen draws the error banner and, beneath it, three pulsing dots that never resolve, with the Save control permanently disabled by `disabled={!groups}` at :188 and no retry short of a manual reload. The failure path reports the failure and then re-enters the loading state it was leaving. CR-16's third clause is the fit: the state left behind claims something that did not happen.

findings.suggestedFix: give the failed load a terminal state of its own — the banner and a retry control, and no preloader, when error is set and groups is null

findings.rule: sweep 11 — a mechanism applied at some call sites and not the rest
findings.claim: the request title's ellipsis is declared on an inline element, where overflow and text-overflow do not apply, so a long title is never truncated — while the screen's two other truncating cells sit on blockified grid items and work

witness.detail: reqTitleStyle (lines 42-48) sets overflow:'hidden', textOverflow:'ellipsis', whiteSpace:'nowrap' and is applied at :89 to a `<b>`, which is display:inline. overflow does not apply to a non-replaced inline box and text-overflow requires a non-visible overflow, so neither declaration does anything; the `<b>` is nested inside the grid item `<span style={{minWidth:0}}>`, so it is not blockified either. TC-01-E2E-08's 200-character title is then laid out on one unbroken nowrap line and paints across the auto due-date cell and the badge to its right until Card's own clip cuts it at the panel edge, with no ellipsis. The same mechanism IS applied correctly twice on this screen, at snameStyle (PortalMonthPanel.tsx:72, on a direct child of a display:grid row) and hnameStyle (PortalTimeOffPanel.tsx:63, likewise), which is why this is CR-18 and not a matter of taste. specs/portal/01-home.mock.html:125 declares the same rule with the missing piece: `.req .t b{…display:block;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}`.

findings.suggestedFix: add display:'block' to reqTitleStyle, as the mock does

findings.rule: sweep 8 — a test cannot fail for the defect it exists to catch
findings.claim: the geometry case seeds one request row per organization and compares the two organizations' single rows, so the content-sized layout the spec names as the failure mode still passes

witness.detail: portal.spec.ts:353-354 asserts toHaveCount(1) on portal-request-row in both organizations, then :356-363 passes the first row's `<b>` from each page to expectSharedEdge. Both requests are raised by a colleague onto the admin with no neededBy, so both rows draw the identical 'Open' badge, and both pages run at the project's 1280px viewport. Now suppose PortalRequestsPanel were built the way contracts §Geometry & motion warns against — 'Drawn the other way round — badge first — every row starts its title at a different x, because each row's first column is sized by its own content'. The long row's title would start at badge-width + gap and the short row's at exactly the same x, because the badge string is the same in both organizations; expectSharedEdge sees one distinct edge and passes. The case's Expected Result is 'the request title's left edge is identical across every row' — across rows of differing length inside one organization, which is the comparison that discriminates, and with one row per organization that clause is vacuously true. F9 is the proof that this case cannot see what it is for: the title's truncation is broken today and TC-01-E2E-08 passes.

findings.suggestedFix: seed at least two requests per organization with markedly different title lengths, and two project rows likewise, and pass every row's locator to expectSharedEdge so the invariant is proven within one organization as the case states

The feed is untouched — it answers a different question. |' page.tsx:167 passes `canManageSettings={homeState.status === 'ready' && homeState.data.canManageSettings}`, so both the error and the loading states hand the feed `false`. An admin opens /org/{orgId}, GET .../portal/home answers 500, the left column draws the banner and the feed column draws no settings link — the only control the feed carries, and the only route to the screen that explains an empty group (REQ-01-037's Decided note). Nothing forces the dependency: REQ-01-052 gates the control on manage-portal-settings, which is derivable from the session the shell already holds through hasCapability(normalizeRole(session.role), 'ManagePortalSettings'), exactly as Sidebar.tsx gates every row.

findings.rule: contracts vs cases — what `link` carries on a project entry
findings.claim: `link` is hardcoded null for every project entry and every reader, while the contract ties link to REQ-01-047 and TC-01-INT-18 pins it only for the unassigned reader

witness.detail: contracts: 'link carries the in-app destination the reader may open — /org/{orgId}/members/{id} on a person's entry, null where the reader may open nothing (REQ-01-047)'. TC-01-INT-18: 'the unassigned reader's carries no roster, no client and link: null'. Known Gaps says only that a user can open no project screen. The three do not settle what an assigned reader or a manage-projects holder is answered, so the implementation's choice is unguarded either way.

findings.suggestedFix: state in the document whether a reader holding REQ-01-047's test is answered a project link, or that link is null for the kind outright

findings.claim: the personal half filters status 'open' alone, while the requests area treats ['open','answered'] as the live span, so the two screens can answer a different count for the same person on the same day

witness.detail: portal-home.service.ts:336 filters `status: 'open'`. apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:260 and :265 count a member's live requests with `status: { in: ['open','answered'] }`, and :131, :144, :153 treat both as non-terminal. REQ-01-020 says 'open requests' without naming the statuses.

findings.suggestedFix: say in the document which statuses the panel spans; if both, use the same span the requests area uses

findings.claim: the rail's logo still addresses /org/{orgId}/members after the organization root became the home screen, so the shell now offers two different 'home' destinations

witness.detail: Sidebar.tsx:303 passes logoHref={`/org/${orgId}/members`} to the Rail, unchanged by this diff, while REQ-01-001 moves the landing to /org/{orgId} and REQ-01-003 puts Team overview first in the rail pointing at the same root. Nothing in the bundle asks for the logo to move — contracts §Screens says only that 'The login form changes its destination and nothing else' — so this is for a person, not a defect against a rule.

findings.suggestedFix: none in this run; a person decides whether the logo follows the landing, in a document

findings.rule: sweep 11 — a mechanism applied at some call sites and not the rest
findings.claim: the settings pair answers a bare 403 where every other route in this spec answers 404 for the same state — a session whose account holds no active membership in this organization

witness.detail: resolvePortalCaller (portal-entry.types.ts:163) and PortalHomeService.requireMembership (portal-home.service.ts:164) both throw NotFoundException on `!membership || status !== 'active' || organizationId !== organizationId`; portal-settings.service.ts:150 throws ForbiddenException() on the identical condition, which contradicts contracts §Routes ('403 … a member of this organization without the capability') and §Security. S3 raised this as a blocker on the scenario 'a removed member's cookie still passes SessionGuard'; I checked it and the scenario does not hold — apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:245-248 rotates securityStamp inside the removal transaction, so a removed member's session is dead at SessionGuard, and OrgScopeGuard already answers 404 to a client principal and to a wrong orgId before the service is reached. I could construct no live session that reaches this branch, so it is demoted to a note. It is worth recording because the branch copies RequestTopicsService.requireCaller (apps/api/src/requests/request-topics.service.ts:434-453) verbatim, so the same inconsistency is now in two areas, and it is one reachable state away from being a live refusal-discipline defect.

findings.suggestedFix: throw NotFoundException from the no-active-membership / wrong-organization branch, keeping ForbiddenException(settingsForbidden) for the capability check alone

findings.rule: sweep 11 — a mechanism applied at some call sites and not the rest
findings.claim: the entry page's fetch has no cancellation guard, unlike its sibling on the home screen, so a response for a superseded entryId can write itself into state

witness.detail: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/page.tsx:92-113 wraps its fetch in a `cancelled` flag checked before every setState and cleared in the effect teardown. `load` (news/[entryId]/page.tsx:212-238) has none, and the effect at :240-243 calls it directly. If the component instance is reused across a params change — /org/X/news/A to /org/X/news/B, the same route segment — and A's response lands after B's, the page draws A's title, facts and share URL under B's address. Noted rather than blocked because no in-app path navigates entry to entry in this release: the feed links in, and portal-entry-back and entry.link both lead out.

findings.suggestedFix: carry the same cancelled flag through load's setState calls

findings.rule: sweep 12 — one value with two sources (UI-07)
findings.claim: the entry's stamp is formatted in the browser's timezone while the rest of the portal resolves dates in Account.timezone

witness.detail: formatTimestamp (:186-194) builds an Intl.DateTimeFormat with no timeZone option. An account whose timezone is Europe/Warsaw, read from a browser set to America/Los_Angeles, opens an entry with occurredAt 2026-09-08T00:30:00Z: the home screen's greeting says Tuesday 8 September and the entry page's stamp says 'Monday, 7 September, 17:30'. The spec is silent on this route's zone and the response body carries none, which is why this is a note where F5 is a blocker.

findings.suggestedFix: pass the caller's timezone to Intl.DateTimeFormat on this page

findings.claim: the geometry case reaches its measurement targets by tag name — locator('b') and locator('span').last() — so a structural edit to either panel silently moves the measurement onto a different box

witness.detail: portal.spec.ts:358-359 selects the request title as `getByTestId('portal-request-row').first().locator('b')` and :365-366 the minutes cell as `getByTestId('portal-month-project-row').first().locator('span').last()`. The month row is today `{projectName}{minutes}` (PortalMonthPanel.tsx:135-136), so adding any span moves the assertion onto it while the case keeps passing. A note rather than a blocker because the fix needs two ids the contracts' testid table does not name, and CLAUDE.md forbids a test id the spec does not name — so this cannot be closed in code alone.

findings.suggestedFix: add ids for the title and minutes cells to the contracts' Required data-testid table, then assert against them

findings.claim: the feed's sentence is composed twice, once in the feed and once on the entry page, with nothing holding the copies together

witness.detail: REQ-01-039 requires the entry page to be headed by 'the same sentence the feed drew for it'. feedSentence (PortalFeed.tsx:148-203) composes the four sentences and news/[entryId]/page.tsx:171-183 composes them again from its own literals. feedSentence is not exported, so nothing prevents drift; the contract answers no title field on the entry route, so composing it client-side is what the spec leaves available. They agree today, which is why this is a note.

findings.suggestedFix: export one sentence builder and have both screens read it

findings.claim: the way out of the no-country state points at a screen where the holiday country cannot be stated

witness.detail: 'Set it on your profile →' links to /account/settings. resolveMemberHolidayCountry (packages/validation/src/reports.ts:546-573) resolves the holiday country as the country stated on the membership and nothing else — 'Never a phone country' — and AccountSettingsScreen.tsx:341 carries only a phone country code. A reader who follows the link finds nothing there that changes the sentence they came from. The mock says 'profile' without naming a route, so which destination is right is a product question.

findings.suggestedFix: point at the screen where a membership's country is set, or drop the link

findings.claim: the request badges take a tone the borrow table does not list, and a solid paint where the mock draws a tint

witness.detail: The borrow table names two uses: Badge neutral (§59) for categories and a request's Open state, and Badge warning/error (§32) for Overdue alone. The implementation adds status="info" for 'Waiting on you' (:96) and maps Overdue to status="inactive" (:94), which packages/ds/src/components/core/Badge.tsx:26-27 paints as a solid --status-error with white ink and documents as a person state. The mock draws both as tints (mock:136-138). No new colour is invented, so this is a note.

findings.suggestedFix: settle the three request tones against the borrow table

findings.claim: several details the mock draws are absent or reworded, with no record of the decision

witness.detail: Against mock:341-352 the proportion bar on each project row (.sbar) is not drawn, and the caption reads 'Tracked this month' where the mock reads 'Tracked in September'; PortalTimeOffPanel.tsx:125 draws 'Next holidays · PL' where the mock draws 'Next holidays · Poland'. The mock's third figure ('Yesterday') is correctly omitted — the contract's home body carries no such field — but the bar is derivable from minutes / totalMinutes, which the body does carry. Also: formatDurationHuman (packages/validation/src/index.ts:2628) returns '4h 5m' unpadded where §Geometry & motion writes '4h 05m'; tabular-nums still aligns the columns, so the glyph count simply differs from the one the table reasoned about. None of these is a rule in §Screens or §Geometry & motion, so each is a note.

findings.suggestedFix: draw the bar and the country name and pad the minutes, or record in the spec that they were dropped

findings.claim: a dozen size literals beyond the two the DS gaps table records reach app code, and the subject tile is a control the design system does not have, written twice on screens

witness.detail: contracts §DS gaps records exactly two: --feed-col and the '32px / var(--font-weight-light)' figure pair. Also written as literals: the 8px holiday dot and 74px date column (PortalTimeOffPanel.tsx:56-58, :50), the 36px feed tile and 32px gear and letterSpacing 0.06em (PortalFeed.tsx:128-129, :32-33, :48), gap 2px and letterSpacing -0.5px (PortalMonthPanel.tsx:37, :46), lineHeight 1.6 and maxWidth 34ch (PortalFeed.tsx:373), maxWidth 720 (settings/portal/page.tsx:139), and the 40px subject tile here and in PortalFeed — which the mock sizes at 56 on the entry head (mock:231) and 36 in the feed (mock:156), so the head is drawn at neither. '1px solid var(--border-subtle)' (PortalRequestsPanel.tsx:37, PortalTimeOffPanel.tsx:29) is spelled 'var(--border-width-hairline)' in settings/portal/page.tsx:155, so one hairline is written two ways inside one change. I considered blocking under CR-11 and did not: the register's remedy is to add the value to the design system and record it in the spec's DS gaps table, and the implementer may not edit a spec, so routing this to `code` cannot terminate. It goes to a person instead. The 400px feed column is NOT part of this — it is spec-mandated and is the first row of the DS gaps table.

findings.suggestedFix: spell the hairline one way, size the entry head's tile and Avatar as the mock does, and add DS gaps rows (or tokens) for whichever of these the next screen would copy

findings.rule: contracts §Validation Rules — the limit the client ships
findings.claim: the feed ships no limit, where the contract says the client ships one as a constant

witness.detail: contracts §Validation Rules: 'The client validates nothing on the read routes — it never composes a cursor by hand, and the limit is a constant it ships.' fetchPage builds the query as `cursor ? '?cursor=…' : ''` and never sends limit, relying on the server default of 20. Behaviour is identical today; the divergence is that the page size is now a server constant the screen cannot see.

findings.suggestedFix: send the limit the screen means, or amend the contract sentence

findings.claim: the reserve block re-implements VacationService's balance arithmetic as a second copy rather than calling the shipped one

witness.detail: portal-home.service.ts:254-285 duplicates apps/api/src/vacation/vacation.service.ts:224-249 (loadRequests), :362-371 (currentYearBalance) and :379-400 (buildBalance) in effect — the current-year transaction sum, the approved/pending aggregation by startDate year, and calculateAvailableDays with the pending hold. The two agree today and nothing keeps them agreeing; a change to the vacation rule now has to be found in two files, and the home screen would keep answering the old number.

findings.suggestedFix: extract the aggregation once and call it from both, or state in the document that the portal owns its own copy

dismissedClaims.claim: app-shell.spec.ts:28 was flipped from aria-expanded 'true' to 'false', so the app-shell rule that 'a group that becomes current opens itself' is now proven nowhere
dismissedClaims.why: Checked and it does not hold. e2e/tests/hiring-vacancies.spec.ts:85-98 covers exactly that rule and was not touched by this change: it does `page.goto('/org/{orgId}/hiring/vacancies/{id}')` — a deep link with no nav click — then asserts the Hiring group is aria-expanded 'true', nav-vacancies carries aria-current='page', People is 'false' and nav-members is absent. The child's own grep listed those lines and misread them as not being nav groups. The flip in app-shell.spec.ts is correct for the new landing and removes no coverage.

dismissedClaims.claim: the inline 'Something went wrong' banners are not CR-07, because CR-07 covers only validation messages and the contracts' Error Messages table words no failure banner
dismissedClaims.why: Overturned; kept as F4. The register's own wording is 'a user-facing message is written inline rather than taken from a packages/validation export', not 'a validation message', and the measured convention is unanimous: every one of the ten 'Something went wrong' strings that already ships is a packages/validation export, and all seven inline occurrences in apps/web are this change's own. That the contracts' table words no failure banner is the defect's cause, not its excuse.

dismissedClaims.claim: a removed member's cookie still passes SessionGuard, so the settings pair's 403 is a live refusal-discipline defect
dismissedClaims.why: The scenario does not hold: apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:245-248 rotates securityStamp inside the removal transaction, so the session is dead at SessionGuard. Demoted to note N10, where the inconsistency is still recorded.

dismissedConcerns: The 30 rewritten e2e waits could still match the old landing and so be unable to fail — /\/org\/[^/]+\/?$/ cannot match '/org/{id}/members', since [^/]+ spans no second segment and \/?$ anchors at the end.

The four surviving waitForURL('**/members') calls — signup.spec.ts:16 is the signup redirect (SignupForm.tsx:101, which Out of Scope leaves alone), request-topics.spec.ts:372 is an unauthorized reader's router.replace (settings/request-topics/page.tsx:55), and time-tracking.spec.ts:116 and invitation.spec.ts:57 follow a real navigation.
responsive.spec.ts navigating to members before reading page-title — the case previously landed on members, so it asserts the same thing in the same place; not a relaxation.

hasCapability being handed the raw role at portal-entry.types.ts:165 — packages/validation/src/roles.ts:318-320 normalizes internally, so the legacy `member` value reads as `user` and TC-01-INT-02 exercises it (CR-04 clean).

The roster query at portal-entry.service.ts:306 not scoping by organizationId — the project it keys on was loaded at :90 with `where: { id, organizationId }`, so the scope is already proven (CR-01 clean).

The `PORTAL_MESSAGES.noProject` literal still written inline in reports.service.ts — contracts §Error Messages states the decision explicitly ('This spec does not change that call site; it declines to copy the literal a second time'), and the static gate already recorded it as a note.
The 400px feed column — contracts §Layout mandates 'a fixed 400px' and the DS gaps table's first row records it.
Accepting an invitation still landing on /members — specs/portal/README.md, Backward Compatibility: 'The only edits outside /portal are the sidebar's new row and the login form's destination string.'
The portal home carrying no `page-title` testid — PageTitle overrides it with portal-greeting, and reports/page.tsx:76 does the same with reports-landing-title.
A test pinning a port or naming devscribed_dev — none in any of the 63 files (CR-28 clean).
apps/web gaining a route handler or a server action, or a fetch without credentials — all four new fetches carry credentials: 'same-origin' and both new pages are 'use client' (CR-10 clean).

The migration — one CREATE TABLE, one unique index, one cascading FK, no backfill, nothing renamed or dropped and no existing column made NOT NULL; previously deployed code never selects a table it does not know about (CR-21, CR-22 clean).

The test-support fixture — behind this.guard, which is the shared assertFixturesOpen plus the in-memory mail-sink check, exactly as the contract says; and its 'Membership.accountId is @unique' comment is true (schema.prisma:244).
